parsed.explanation: Strong institutional protections: gender identity/expression protected nationally (human-rights act, hate-crime provisions, 2017), documented human-rights-complaint routes, and a national custody rule placing prisoners by gender identity — a positive, not a liability. No traveler-facing exposure is documented: no border/screening friction, no facility bans, no presentation offence. Weigh against this: police-reported hate crimes rose 169% since 2018 (though the series is not trans-disaggregated — magnitude of anti-trans targeting unresolved, and 90% of surveyed violence was verbal), a rising organised anti-trans movement, and two provinces' school-pronoun/healthcare rollbacks. These are climate signals and resident/minor-facing measures, not visitor exposures; the 2022 abuse-in-jails report is concerning but contested by an officer study finding attention to trans safety, and custodial entry is rare for visitors. Low-risk band with deductions for the deteriorating social climate and unresolved violence data.
